triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100) risks the '9. `.item()` is a structural barrier (and CUPTI *does* see it); `tensor.shape` is free' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA B200 (GB200 / SM100): 9. `.item()` is a structural barrier (and CUPTI *does* see it); `tensor.shape` is free

problem.statement: sm_100 Triton sparse-decode / split-K pitfalls -- 9. `.item()` is a structural barrier (and CUPTI *does* see it); `tensor.shape` is free

payload.attempted: Read a GPU-derived scalar (e.g. `num_valid.item()`) on the launch path to pick a kernel variant. "It's a cheap reduction."
payload.lesson: Never put `.item()` on a hot launch path. **Host-known shapes are free**: `max_num_pages = block_table.shape[1]` is a plain Python int (no sync), so branch on *shape* predicates (`if max_num_pages == 1: fast_path()`) to dispatch specialized kernels at ~0.3 µs cost. To dispatch on *data* properties without a sync, keep the decision on-device (launch max splits + self-skip empty work).

established_fact.mechanism: `.item()` is a device→host sync on the default stream, not just a copy — the whole pipeline drains.

payload.observed: A `.item()` before launch added **~60 µs** serial stall on a 12-µs workload (~9× blowup) — it blocks the CPU until *all* prior stream work finishes, then gates dispatch of the next kernel. Moving it *after* the launch still stalls ~30 µs (gates the following kernel). Unlike CUDA-graph overlap, this **is** visible to a CUPTI harness because it serializes the queue.
payload.root_cause: `.item()` is a device→host sync on the default stream, not just a copy — the whole pipeline drains.
